assign.card: Cards: a sub-card opens in a column beside its parent

log.msg: minion skill loaded. Read requirements.md. Plan: read card.js, Inbox/Rail.js, Card.css, Inbox.css; flatten the mount so every depth joins one shared row (shell.$sub), show only last two boxes at equal width via Card.seam() divider, breadcrumb for hidden ancestors, keep narrow fallback. Test with a 2-deep card chain, layout-check.mjs at 4 widths, back/forward/reload, then merge.mjs.

decision.what: kept the top-level card mounted in .inbox-detail unchanged (brief's 'leave as is if simpler' option); only the sub-card chain inside shell.$sub became the flat row that slides its visible window
decision.alt: move the top-level card into the same flat row as every sub-card too — rejected: that mount decision is made by Router.container() walking up to the SHELL page's own $pages (set once in Rail.mount for every Inbox consumer, not just Card), before Card.content() ever runs, so redirecting it would mean changing shared Rail.js behavior for every non-Card consumer too

log.msg: found (by reading core/Page/Page.class.js container()) that a sub-card's children already flatten into shell.$sub today via the walk-up-to-the-nearest-ancestor-with-$pages rule, even before my edit — the brief's own words ('a sub-card does not get this treatment, its children nest inside its own box') describes the SYMPTOM (today only the single deepest one is ever visible, via the generic active-ancestor-hidden-by-a-later-sibling contract in core/Page/Page.css) not the DOM structure, which was already flat. Changed the content() line anyway (now applies at every depth, not just !sub) so the mounting target is stated explicitly rather than relying on an implicit walk two files away — same end state, clearer code.

decision.what: used CSS :nth-last-child(-n+2 of .active-page, .active-ancestor) to pick the last two open levels inside .inbox-sub, found via core/new/1/site/versus/css/page.js — prior research in this repo that proves this exact selector against this exact engine for 'only the last N of a chain' (ColumnPager's problem, which is this task's problem)
decision.alt: track depth/visibility in JS (a counter on the shell, stamped classes on mount) — rejected: the router already marks the whole active chain with .active-page/.active-ancestor on every navigation (back, forward, reload all included for free), and the generic arrangement contract in core/Page/Page.css already proves the pattern of overriding that contract from a more specific util-layer rule, so a second JS-driven visibility system would duplicate state the router already tracks correctly

decision.what: breadcrumb: built in a new Card.breadcrumb() method, called for every sub-card (walks this.parent while instanceof Card, oldest ancestor first); shown via CSS only on the ancestor card that is currently visible as the EARLIER of the two columns (wide screen) or on the one card showing at all (narrow screen) — never on the deepest/active-page card on a wide screen, since its own content fills the second column instead
decision.alt: recompute the breadcrumb on every activation from the current leaf only — rejected: a card's own ancestor chain never changes once built (ancestry is structural), so building it once per card in content() and letting CSS decide which card's copy is currently the one 'in front' avoids any need to re-run JS on every navigation

log.msg: oldest-ancestor-first order picked for the breadcrumb (reads like a familiar left-to-right folder path, CLAUDE.md 'clarity is familiar structure'), over newest-first.
